title: SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX and COUNT
explanation: Here's a week of step counts from a fitness app. Adding cells with + gets slow when there are lots of them. **Functions** are ready-made formulas that do common jobs for you, like adding up a whole column in one go.

tasks.prompt: In E2, add up all the steps with SUM.
tasks.teach: A function has a **name**, then **round brackets** with what it works on inside. `=SUM(B2:B8)` adds up every cell in the range B2 to B8. Remember, B2:B8 means B2 through B8.
hints: The steps are in B2 to B8.

tasks.prompt: In E3, work out the average steps per day with AVERAGE.
tasks.teach: **AVERAGE** works the same way as SUM: the name, then the range in brackets. It adds the cells up and divides by how many there are.
hints: Same range as SUM, different name.

tasks.prompt: In E4, find the best day (the most steps) with MAX.
tasks.teach: **MAX** gives the biggest number in a range, and **MIN** gives the smallest.

tasks.prompt: In E5, find the worst day (the fewest steps) with MIN.
In E6, count how many days have a step count, with COUNT.
tasks.teach: **COUNT** counts how many cells in a range hold **numbers**. It skips empty cells and text. (Its cousin **COUNTA** counts every cell that isn't empty, text included.)
hints: COUNT works on the same range.

tasks.prompt: The app missed a walk on Saturday: it was really 16400 steps. Change B7 to 16400, then look at E2. The total should update by itself.
tasks.teach: This is why formulas beat typing answers in: change one number, and everything that uses it updates instantly.
hints: Click B7 (Saturday), type 16400 and press Enter.
Then look at E2: its SUM updates on its own to 67250.

tasks.prompt: Last one: in E7, work out the range: the best day minus the worst day. Use MAX and MIN in one formula.
tasks.teach: You can use several functions in one formula, with maths between them, like `=MAX(...)-MIN(...)`.
hints: Start with =MAX(B2:B8), then subtract MIN of the same range.

recap: SUM adds up, AVERAGE gives the average, MAX and MIN give the biggest and smallest, and COUNT counts the numbers in a range. Functions update by themselves when the data changes.
